summary.text: A 34-year-old woman, G4 L2 Ab1, who had married her cousin, had two prior normal vaginal deliveries and one first-trimester abortion. Using withdrawal contraception, she had no menstruation during breastfeeding and 6 months after her last pregnancy, and a pregnancy test was requested. The positive result led to an ultrasound study showing a 10-week spontaneous gestation with 4 gestational sacs and 4 fetuses, with no family history of multiple pregnancies.

She received prenatal care without prophylactic cerclage. She was hospitalized at week 24 for premature contractions, controlled with pethidine and hydration, and discharged 3 days later. At 28 weeks she was admitted again with similar contractions and treated with indomethacin and pethidine; she also received two doses of betamethasone during hospitalization. A week later she was admitted with labour contractions and given tocolytics.

Fetal health was monitored by Doppler ultrasound imaging, biophysical profile and non stress test, and she was monitored in hospital up to delivery. At 32 weeks and 4 days, after a rescue dose of betamethasone, cesarean section and tubectomy delivered four neonates. Atonic uterus was treated with oxytocin, methylergonovine, rectal misoprostol, uterine artery blocking and a B-Lynch suture, without blood transfusion.

The four neonates weighed between 1810 and 2100 gram with Apgar scores from 6-7 to 9-10, and only quadruplet B went to the NICU, being discharged after 2 days. The mother was discharged 3 days after delivery without complications. Mother and newborns were healthy two weeks after delivery, and the infants showed normal physical and mental development at 6 months.
